correctness.rationale: For the exact labelled 90-point fiber, Walsh Gram entries equal summed binary Krawtchouk polynomials by a direct character-intersection count. Two standalone integer programs independently enumerate the locus (six row patterns versus all 65536 bit arrays), reconstruct degree-zero-to-four matrices, and reproduce the exact characteristic factors and rank sequence. The 137-column quadratic Gram spectrum, 90 normalization, and Hilbert filtration follow from exact linear algebra and invertible Walsh/monomial triangular basis change. Only this finite case is proved.

originality.rationale: The 2006 and 2010 primary literature treats counting, sampling, and asymptotic structure of fixed-margin binary matrices but not the exact low-degree Fourier interpolation spectrum. A 2025 paper on orbit harmonics of nonnegative-integer contingency tables expressly poses the binary fixed-margin orbit-harmonics locus as an open direction. The present specific Hilbert series and six-level quadratic spectrum are not implied by its nonnegative-integer formula. value.rationale: A canonically constrained 90-point 4-by-4 half-density fiber is the first nontrivial balanced-square example of a binary fixed-margin orbit-harmonics locus, an explicit research direction in Oh–Rhoades Problem 7.4. The exact graded Hilbert series and minimal Fourier interpolation degree, together with the independent quadratic Gram stability spectrum, are intrinsic and reusable benchmarks; these values are not generic consequences of fixed row/column sums or classical counting. This is a meaningful finite result, not an all-dimensions theorem.
